implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines' Channel is the idiomatic work queue, and close() is documented as sending a special close token: receivers keep draining already-sent elements, after which a regular for (msg in channel) loop ends, with receiveCatching()/onClosed available when the closure reason matters. One close terminates every receiver of that channel, and cancelling a producer coroutine - or letting produce's block finish - closes the channel automatically, which replaces per-consumer pill bookkeeping. The classic Java-style BlockingQueue plus a poison object remains the option when consumers are plain JVM threads rather than coroutines.
pitfalls: Sending on a closed channel fails (send throws ClosedSendChannelException, trySend returns a failure); close from the producer side only.
consumeEach cancels the channel when one consumer finishes, silently starving the other fan-out consumers - use a plain for-loop in fan-out.
close() still delivers buffered elements to receivers, but cancelling the consumer coroutine discards them; distinguish stopping the producer from cancelling the consumers.
A rendezvous channel (capacity 0) makes close() delivery depend on receivers being scheduled, so a shutdown that closes while receivers are stalled can suspend senders.
